If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test exercises
  - The test runs BOBYQA on a 13D constrained Rosenbrock function, varying the number of interpolation points from m = 15 + num, with num in [1, 47], i.e., m in [16, 62].
  - The algorithm should accept any m in [n + 2, (n + 1)(n + 2)/2] = [15, 105] for n = 13. In particular, it should support values greater than 2n + 1 = 27. The comment notes failures at specific m values (48, 59, 62, …), which are within the valid range.

- Relevant setup in the code
  - BOBYQAOptimizer.setup(double[], double[]) validates m and allocates:
    - interpolationPoints = new Array2DRowRealMatrix(numberOfInterpolationPoints, dimension);
    - Other matrices sized consistently with n = dimension and m = numberOfInterpolationPoints.
  - So interpolationPoints has m rows and n columns. Any access must use a column index in [0, n − 1].

- Where the error occurs
  - The issue report points to a failure around line 1662 in BOBYQAOptimizer, at a statement:
    interpolationPoints.setEntry(nfm, ipt, interpolationPoints.getEntry(ipt, ipt));
  - Although that exact snippet is not shown above, it is consistent with the initialization phase inside the bobyqa method (called from doOptimize) that builds the initial interpolation set when m > 2n + 1.

- Why it fails when m exceeds 2n + 1
  - In the initialization, for m ≤ 2n + 1, only “axial” interpolation points along ± coordinate directions are used. Indices that double as both interpolation point indices and coordinate indices stay less than n, so misuse of an index is masked.
  - For m > 2n + 1, the algorithm begins adding extra points corresponding to pairs of coordinates. At that point, variables like ipt (which name suggests “interpolation point index”) can take values up to m − 1, which can be ≥ n.
  - The offending line uses ipt as a column index (second argument of setEntry and getEntry) into interpolationPoints, but the number of columns is n (the problem dimension). When ipt ≥ n (which happens only when m is large enough to enter the “extra points” branch), this produces an out-of-range column index and triggers an exception.
  - In other words, a variable representing an interpolation point index is mistakenly used as a coordinate index. This is a translation bug (likely from the original 1-based FORTRAN code), where the intended column index should be a true coordinate index (0..n − 1) such as i or j, or an adjusted form (e.g., ipt − offset), not ipt itself.

- Why only some m values fail in the test
  - The faulty statement is reached only for particular (ipt, jpt, …) combinations during the enumeration of extra interpolation points. For some m values, the iteration hits a state where ipt ≥ n and the bad access occurs; for others inside the tested range it may not get to that offending access before finishing the initialization. Hence the observed failures at specific totals (48, 59, 62, …) rather than a uniform failure for all m > 2n + 1.
  - This also matches the report that “anything larger than 2*dim+1 causes an error” in practical runs: once the extra-point branch is required, the incorrect index mixing is very likely to be exercised.

- Summary of root cause
  - In BOBYQAOptimizer.bobyqa(…), during the construction of the initial interpolation set for m > 2n + 1, the code mixes up interpolation point indices with coordinate indices. Specifically, it uses ipt (an interpolation point row index) as a column index into interpolationPoints, whose columns are bounded by the problem dimension n. This leads to out-of-bounds matrix access and failure.
  - The fix is to use the correct coordinate index variable for the column (staying in [0, n − 1]), or to apply the proper offset/translation when deriving a coordinate index from ipt, instead of using ipt directly.
